extracted.intended_audience: graduate students, scholars, and advanced readers of narratology and literary criticism (especially Proust studies)
extracted.subtask_description: Analytic criteria for recognizing, classifying, and assessing retrospective (analepsis) and anticipatory (prolepsis) narrative operations, their functions, and techniques of junction/resumption, with Proustian examples. Focused on how temporal displacements produce meaning, voice effects, and narrative structure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Migration / narrative scattering
rubrics_metrics.description: Instances in which material (memories, information) seems 'snatched' from another part of the text and relocated — described as migration or narrative scattering.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recognize passages that appear displaced from their chronological context; treat them as migratory insertions that reconfigure narrative texture (example: a passage about Rachel's past conduct appearing as if snatched from another section).

rubrics_metrics.name: Recalls modify past occurrences retroactively
rubrics_metrics.description: Recalls frequently 'modify the meaning of past occurrences after the event,' either by making significant what had been insignificant or by refuting an initial interpretation and replacing it with a new one.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate recalls for their retrospective function — do they bestow new significance, overturn earlier readings, or both? (Examples throughout the Recherche; quoted narratorial formulations signal this modality.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Deferred or postponed significance (principle of deferred significance)
rubrics_metrics.description: Events that seemed unimportant at the time are later endowed with significance (deferred interpretation), often explicitly signalled by the narrator.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify narratorial signals of deferred interpretation (e.g. 'At the actual moment, I saw nothing...') and trace how later information (Andree's revelation, Albertine's death) retroactively transforms meaning; this device aligns with Barthes' mechanism of enigma.

rubrics_metrics.name: Double narrative / naive then enlightened viewpoint
rubrics_metrics.description: A situation is told first from a naive (earlier) viewpoint and later from an enlightened (later) viewpoint, the latter supplying the clue that dissipates earlier confusion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat paired accounts as a single narrative strategy (first perception, later interpretation). Example: the syringas incident told first through Marcel's ignorance, later clarified by Andree and Albertine.

rubrics_metrics.name: Delayed identification as normative device
rubrics_metrics.description: Characters or elements encountered earlier are revealed much later to be significant figures (e.g. 'the Lady in pink', Duc de Bouillon), making delayed identification a background norm in the text.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Note how frequent delayed identifications build suspense and structure (sometimes used so often it becomes the norm; absence of identification can be used for contrast). Examples: many small figures later turn out to be notable persons.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reinterpretation of events (reversal from pro to con)
rubrics_metrics.description: Events that already had a meaning when they occurred later receive a different (not always better) interpretation, facilitating continual 'reversal from pro to con' typical of Proustian apprenticeship to truth.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Track sequences of revelations/confessions that dissolve and reform retrospective images (Odette, Gilberte, Albertine, Saint-Loup) and evaluate how reinterpretation circulates meaning within the novel.

rubrics_metrics.name: Determination of reach: external vs internal analepses
rubrics_metrics.description: Analepses are divided by reach depending on whether the point to which they reach lies outside or inside the temporal field of the first narrative (external vs internal).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Classify a retrospection by locating its temporal target relative to the 'first narrative' frame: outside => external; inside => internal. Use reach to decide which class applies (with examples drawn from the Odyssey comparisons).

rubrics_metrics.name: Extent controls mixed class: extent vs reach
rubrics_metrics.description: A mixed class of analepses is determined by extent: external analepses prolonged to rejoin and pass beyond the starting point of the first narrative; extent may equal or exceed reach and controls classification.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Measure both reach (temporal point targeted) and extent (how much of intervening time is covered) to classify analepses as mixed, internal-complete, etc. Example: Des Grieux's narrative is mixed because extent rejoins beyond the original starting point.

rubrics_metrics.name: Partial analepsis (pinpointed retrospection)
rubrics_metrics.description: A partial analepsis recounts an isolated past moment and ends on an ellipsis without rejoining the first narrative; it serves to supply a specific piece of information necessary for a present scene.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use partial analepses when a single past fact is required for understanding the present (example: Ulysses' wound episode); expect a clear interruption and then resumption of the first narrative.

rubrics_metrics.name: Complete analepsis (full retrospection)
rubrics_metrics.description: A complete analepsis goes back to an origin point (e.g., fall of Troy) and carries the narrative forward to rejoin the first narrative without a gap; it retrieves the antecedents and can form a major part of the narrative.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify long retrospections that re-cover the intervening period and reunite with the present scene; these often serve the practice of beginning in medias res and can even function as the chief part of the story.

rubrics_metrics.name: Complete internal analepsis / extent equals reach
rubrics_metrics.description: A 'complete internal' analepsis rejoins the first narrative not at its beginning but at the exact point where the first was interrupted; in such cases extent is rigorously equal to reach (perfect round trip).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Detect narratives that circle back precisely to the interruption point (examples: Les Souffrances de l'inventeur, Des Grieux's narrative) and treat them as structurally self-contained round trips.

rubrics_metrics.name: Resumption types: explicit (Balzacian 'this is why') vs discreet/elliptical
rubrics_metrics.description: Resumptions (returns from analepsis to the first narrative) may be explicit and signalled by formulas ('this is why') or may be discreet/elliptical, sometimes marked only by a paragraph break or minimal phrase.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate how the author signals resumption: explicit signals foreground explanatory function; elliptical resumptions create temporal rupture by understatement and can require attentive reading to locate the leap.

rubrics_metrics.name: Elliptical resumption as asyndeton (temporal rupture by understatement)
rubrics_metrics.description: Elliptical resumptions may use no explicit linking (sometimes only a paragraph break), underlining the temporal rupture by asyndeton and making the transition less perceptible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Look for minimal or absent connective phrasing at the end of analepses; interpret the effect as emphasizing rupture or continuity by omission (examples: Vinteuil sonata recall → paragraph break).

rubrics_metrics.name: Junction/overlap problem with completing analepses
rubrics_metrics.description: Completing analepses that must rejoin the first narrative can produce awkward overlaps unless the narrator skillfully transforms the awkwardness into charm or decorative effect.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether the junction creates incoherence (awkward jump) or is handled playfully (e.g., Les Souffrances de l'inventeur extracting a decorative element); maladroit linking (Cesar Birotteau example) signals poor junction management.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eluding the juncture (Proustian technique)
rubrics_metrics.description: Proust often eludes acknowledging the end of an analepsis by dissimulating it through iterative narrative dispersion, pretending ignorance of the prior point, or simply omitting overt linkage.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recognize strategies that avoid signaling the analepsis' end — dissimulation, continuation without acknowledgment, or feigned oversight — and consider how this affects perceived continuity and narratorial footprints.

rubrics_metrics.name: Forgetting analeptic character / prolonged retrospection becomes anticipatory
rubrics_metrics.description: Sometimes the narrator forgets the analeptic nature of a section and prolongs it without signaling its rejoining point, covertly transforming a retrospection into an anticipation or into a new narrative level.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When a retrospective section continues past its originating occasion (example: grandmother's death; the large analepsis beginning in 'Noms de pays'), treat the transformation into anticipatory or omnitemporal narration as a deliberate destabilization of normative narration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prolepses: internal vs external anticipations
rubrics_metrics.description: Prolepses (anticipations) are classed as internal or external depending on whether the forecasted events lie within or beyond the temporal field of the first narrative; external prolepses often function as epilogues.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Classify anticipatory passages by their temporal relation to the frame; note that in the Recherche many external prolepses continue lines of action to logical conclusions beyond the Guermantes matinee.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prolepses that invoke the narrator's present (voice effect)
rubrics_metrics.description: Anticipations that bring the narrating instance into play (references to 'to-day' or the narrator's present) serve both temporal and voice functions, authenticating memory and blending narrating time with narrated events.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate prolepses not only for temporal function but for their effect on voice: present-tense attestations ('I can see all that departing crowd now') explicitly involve the narrating consciousness and produce omnitemporality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Completing vs repeating prolepses (within homodiegetic anticipations)
rubrics_metrics.description: Among homodiegetic prolepses distinguish completing prolepses (which fill in future blanks ahead of time) from repeating prolepses (which slightly double a narrative section to come).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When analysing anticipations, decide whether the prolepsis is meant to offset future ellipses (completing) or to echo/duplicate forthcoming narrative material (repeating); examples cited include school years, future dinner-series, and erotic sequels.
